name: Thread (IEEE 802.15.4)
label: Thread
notes: Thread frames on IEEE 802.15.4, decoded by OnAir's receiver (the Zigbee receiver in its Thread mode) through the onair-rx handler; the row has no decoder of its own, so only a handler runs it. One job reads one channel: start it on a 2.4 GHz channel's centre with a band of 2 MHz (the handler takes 4 MHz of IQ, OnAir's minimum). Each event is a frame whose check sequence passed: `frame_type`, `seq`, `pan` (4 hex digits), `src` and `dst` (4 hex digits for a short address, 16 for an extended one; null on a frame with none), `secured` (the link layer is: MAC security, or an AES-CCM level OnAir says is encrypted) and `kind`, OnAir's own sentence for what the frame is (a beacon with its network name, an encrypted data frame, a 6LoWPAN IPHC frame with its MLE command): opaque text, not a vocabulary. Thread has no Zigbee network layer, so there is no `nwk_src` or `nwk_dst`. Nothing is decrypted and no key is loaded; each PSDU with its FCS (link type 195) goes to a packet capture. Ranges and bands: Thread runs on IEEE 802.15.4's 2.4 GHz channels 11 to 26 only (2405 MHz plus 5 MHz a channel, 2 MHz wide), which are also OnAir's Thread tuning; identify and classify try the row inside 2400 to 2483.5 MHz. Listing bar: measured on the build host (12 cores) through a scratch node's release build, 30 s of the generated capture looping on a file source and fed in real time; the job skipped no input, onair-rx used 0.57 of a core and the node 0.28 of a core (load average 5.1 to 4.6, with another build running).
